newsitem.title: SWEDEN: P&U says Biotech unit not for sale.
newsitem.headline: P&U says Biotech unit not for sale.

text.p: Swedish/U.S. drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn said on Monday it was looking for a partner for its Pharmacia Biotech Unit but denied newspaper reports that the division was for sale.

"What's happened is that we want to find strategic cooperation for Biotech, and we have asked (investment bank) Credit Suisse First Boston to help us with that," P&U spokesman Jacob Kaluski told Reuters.
Kaluski said a report in Swedish daily newspaper Dagens Nyheter that the unit was for sale was incorrect.
"As a part of this process we are prepared to go down from our 100 percent ownership, but it's not a question of a sale. We want to be flexible," he said.
Kalusiki declined to comment on how far P&U would be prepared to reduce its ownership or in which areas cooperation would be focused.
Dagens Nyheter said the sale would be arranged by investment bank Credit Suisse First Boston and the asking price would be $500 - 600 million.
The Biotech division, which was once the core of the former Pharmacia before its August 1995 merger with Upjohn, Inc., posted sales of 2.9 billion crowns and a profit of 300 million crowns.
P&U shares were three crowns higher at 241 crowns on the Stockholm bourse at 1215 GMT.
